turns.text: ok it's 100 degrees out and i'm officially a meteorologist now. i have a spreadsheet with tabs for feeds, naps, diapers and 'incidents' and i want to add a heat tab to it. can you help me set up columns for room temperature and how many onesie layers per degree? plus a formula that flags when the nursery gets too warm. he's 5 weeks old, if that matters. please and thanks

Happy to help. A heat tab fits well alongside your other tabs. Quick safety note: the guidance I can give is general, so check the exact comfort range with your pediatrician. Common guidance is to keep a baby's room around 68-72°F (20-22°C).

Suggested columns:

| Col | Header | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| A | Date | |
| B | Time | |
| C | Room temp (°F) | Read from a thermometer at crib height |
| D | Layers | Number of layers worn |
| E | Clothing | Text description |
| F | Status | Formula output |
| G | Notes | Sweaty neck, flushed, fussy, etc. |

Layers per degree, as a starting lookup table (say in I1:J5):

| Room temp (°F) | Suggested layers |
|---|---|
| below 68 | 3 (onesie, sleeper, sleep sack) |
| 68-72 | 2 (onesie plus sleep sack or sleeper) |
| 73-76 | 1 (short-sleeve onesie, light swaddle or none) |
| 77-80 | 1 (just a thin onesie or diaper) |
| above 80 | 0-1, cool the room, check on him often |

Formula for F2 (flag when too warm):

=IF(C2="","",IF(C2>80,"TOO HOT",IF(C2>76,"WARM - lighten up",IF(C2<68,"COOL","OK"))))

For a layers check in column H:

=IF(C2="","",IF(D2>VLOOKUP(C2,$I$1:$J$5,2,TRUE),"Too many layers","OK"))

(Make the lookup table's first column numeric, with the lower bound of each band, e.g. 0, 68, 73, 77, 81, and the second column the max layer count as a number.)

Conditional formatting: select F2:F500 and add rules, red for text containing "TOO HOT", yellow for "WARM".

Want a heat-wave checklist to go with it?

yes please. the evening fussing from like 5 to 8 gets way worse when it's hot so it needs an evening section. also ideally i'd get a temp alert on my phone but the wifi camera monitor keeps dropping whenever the microwave runs 🙃 so i'm not sure i can trust it. short version if possible, i'm typing one-handed

No problem, short version.

**Morning (before it heats up)**
- Close blinds and curtains on sun-facing windows
- Set up fans, aiming to circulate air, not blow directly on him
- Log room temp in your heat tab

**Midday**
- Check room temp every 1-2 hours
- Dress him in 1 light layer, and adjust using your layers table
- Extra feeds are fine; log wet diapers to watch hydration
- Check the back of his neck and chest for sweat or flushing (his hands and feet will feel cooler, so don't go by those)

**Evening (5-8 p.m. fussy stretch)**
- Cool the room before 5, since it's still warmest then
- Lukewarm bath before the crying peaks can help
- Take turns walking him in the coolest part of the home
- Check the temp at the start, and again halfway through
- Note fussiness in column G so you can compare hot and cooler evenings

**Overnight**
- Light sleepwear, nothing loose in the crib
- Check the thermometer before you go to bed and at each feed

**Call the pediatrician if** he has fewer wet diapers than usual, seems unusually sleepy or hard to wake, or feels hot with a flushed face.

**On the monitor:** since the Wi-Fi drops when the microwave runs, don't rely on it alone. A battery-powered thermometer with a display at crib height is a cheap backup. A Bluetooth one avoids Wi-Fi interference and can alert your phone. Also, if the microwave is the culprit, moving the router or monitor farther away from it, or switching the router to 5 GHz, sometimes helps.

Want me to put the checklist into a printable table?
